title: Blizzard Tried to Put Real Names on WoW's Forums. It Lasted 3 Days
hook: In July 2010 Blizzard announced every forum post would show your real name. Its CEO killed the plan three days later. Would you have posted under your real name?
script: Did you know Blizzard once planned to put your real name on every forum post you wrote? On July sixth, twenty ten, Blizzard announced that its official forums would show each poster's real name. The new StarCraft Two forums would get the change first. The World of Warcraft forums would follow with the Cataclysm expansion. Blizzard said the goal was to cut down on trolls and spammers and make the forums more welcoming. Players did not see it that way. Many worried that a full name was enough for a stranger to find their address or their family. The thread about the change pulled in tens of thousands of replies in just three days. On July ninth, Blizzard CEO Mike Morhaime posted a letter to the community. He wrote that real names would not be required for posting on official Blizzard forums. StarCraft Two players would post under their Battle dot net character name and code instead. The new World of Warcraft forums would launch with Cataclysm, also without real names. The optional in game Real ID friends system stayed, but the forum plan was dead after three days. Would you have posted under your real name? Follow for more gaming history.
